department: Department of Integrative Biology (CU Denver College of Liberal Arts and Sciences)

deadline.quote: The annual deadline to apply to our graduate degree programs is January 1.

gre_general.value: Biology graduate programs no longer require GRE scores for admission.
gre_general.quote: NOTE: the Biology graduate programs NO LONGER require GRE scores as part of admission

gre_subject.value: ETS discontinued the Biology GRE Subject Test in May 2021, and Biology no longer requires GRE scores.
gre_subject.quote: NOTE: the Biology graduate programs NO LONGER require GRE scores as part of admission

also.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Prospective graduate students are admitted directly into faculty labs and must contact a prospective advisor in advance to obtain a letter of support.
supervisor.quote: Prospective graduate students are admitted directly into the labs of faculty members. ... A letter of support from your prospective advisor in our program (this will be submitted by them separately)

funding.value: Funding is usually provided through a combination of research grants (GRA), fellowships, and competitive teaching appointments (GTA with salary and tuition benefits).
funding.quote: Financial support for graduate students in biology is usually from a combination of research grants, fellowships, and teaching appointments.

entry_route.value: Apply with a BA/BS awarded in the past 10 years (minimum 3.0 GPA, plus 1 year general biology, 1 year chemistry/physics/math, and statistics).
entry_route.quote: Our MS and PhD programs have the following criteria for admission ... A BA/BS from an accredited institution, awarded in the past 10 years Minimum undergraduate 3.0 GPA

notes: PhD in Integrative and Systems Biology (60 credits, dual-campus CU Denver / Anschutz advising plus affiliate researchers at Denver Botanic Gardens, Denver Museum of Nature & Science, and Denver Zoo).
